readerTitle: Three ideas, one year of savings: which would you chase?
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (청소 회사를 운영했던 창업자 Maya의 아이디어 선택) · 가정 서비스업과 소프트웨어 아이디어 비교 · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 아이디어 선택은 '어느 것이 가장 좋은가'가 아니라 '문제의 증거, 손에 잡히는 시장 크기, 내가 이길 이유' 세 가지를 차례로 거르는 일이다.
misconception: 주변 반응이 가장 좋고 시장이 가장 커 보이는 아이디어를 고르면 된다.

sources.text: ENT-01 유닛 개념 (문제 우선, 시장 규모 추정, 창업자-시장 적합성)
모든 인물, 회사, 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 리노베이션 후 청소: 지역 시공업체 80곳 × 연 10건 × 건당 $400 = $320,000/년. 스케줄링 소프트웨어: 지역 청소업체 300곳 × 월 $60 × 12개월 = $216,000/년. 모두 가상 수치이며 계산을 다시 확인했습니다.
"가정 서비스 예약 사이트가 이미 있다"는 일반적 서술로만 썼고 특정 기업이나 시장 규모 수치는 넣지 않았습니다. 게시 전 표현이 과하지 않은지 확인하세요.

cards.title: Three ideas, one year of savings
body: Maya ran a home cleaning company for eight years, then sold it. She has enough savings to live on for about a year, and three ideas on a notepad.
list: **A home-services app:** book any cleaner, plumber or painter in one place. Her friends love it.
**Scheduling software** for small cleaning companies. She ran her own crews on messy spreadsheets for years.
**After-renovation cleaning** for building contractors in her city. Contractors kept asking if her crews did it.
cards.callout: She can only chase one. You'll decide for her.
cards.softwareNote: Two of the three ideas are digital-friendly, and one is pure software. Notice how the software idea is judged by the same tests as the service ones.

image.label: Three ideas beside a modest savings jar
image.brief: A clay woman at a table with a savings jar and three idea objects.

cards.title: How should Maya narrow the list first?
body: She can't test all three properly. Which filter should come first?

options.text: Go with the idea her friends liked most
options.feedback: Praise from friends is cheap. None of them complained about finding a plumber, and booking sites for home services already exist. She'd start with enthusiasm, not evidence.

options.text: Keep ideas where she's seen people already spend time or money working around the problem
options.feedback: Cleaning owners fight spreadsheets every week. Contractors already ask for, and pay for, one-off cleanups. Both ideas survive. The app drops out.

options.text: Pick the one that's fastest to launch
options.feedback: Speed helps her learn. But fast to launch isn't the same as wanted, and she might quickly learn that nobody needed it.

cards.title: Say you chose the problem filter. How big is each idea?
body: Two ideas are left: the scheduling software and the after-renovation cleaning.
Maya wants a rough sense of size before she commits. How should she estimate it?

options.text: Quote the total size of the cleaning industry from a report
options.feedback: A giant number says nothing about who she could actually sell to. Both ideas would look huge, so it can't help her choose.

options.text: Count the customers she could reach and what each would pay
options.feedback: Slower, but honest. It shows what's reachable now and how each idea would grow. The next card shows her count.

options.text: Skip it and pick the one she's most excited about
options.feedback: Energy matters in a hard first year. But without a rough count, she could pour her savings into a market too small to live on.

cards.title: Counting from the ground up
cards.callout: Rough guesses, not forecasts. Locally, the service is bigger. But software can sell to cleaning companies in other cities without hiring a single new crew. The service grows one crew at a time.
cards.softwareNote: This is the usual software trade-off: a smaller start, but each new customer costs little to serve, so the reachable market can stretch far beyond one city.

cards.title: Say you counted. Which idea does Maya pursue?

image.label: A fork in the road: a cleaning van one way, a laptop the other
image.brief: 갈림길에 선 여성 창업자. 왼쪽 길 끝에는 청소 장비를 실은 밴, 오른쪽 길 끝에는 일정표가 떠 있는 노트북. 실제 로고나 상표는 넣지 않음. 따뜻한 일러스트 톤.

options.text: The software, because it has the bigger ceiling
options.feedback: The pain is real and she knows it well. But she can't code and has never sold software, so she'd spend savings on developers for a product she can't easily judge.

options.text: The after-renovation cleaning, because it fits what she already does well
options.feedback: She can start next week with crews and contractor contacts she already has. Cash comes in, and running more crews keeps her close to the scheduling problem for later.

options.text: Both at once, to spread the risk
options.feedback: Two half-built businesses on one year of savings. Each gets half her time, and neither gets a fair test.

cards.title: Fit is a head start, not a promise.
body: The cleaning service fits Maya, but it grows one crew at a time. That can be a good business without being a startup built for fast, repeatable growth. Neither is wrong. She should know which one she's choosing.
Fit cuts both ways, too. Her experience could lead her to assume every contractor works like the ones she knows. She still needs to check with **new customers**, not just old friends.

cards.title: Pick ideas with evidence, numbers and fit.
body: Each decision used one idea from this unit:
list: **Decision 1 · Problem before solution:** keep ideas where people already work around a real problem.
**Decision 2 · Sizing a market:** count reachable customers and what they'd pay, from the ground up.
**Decision 3 · Founder-market fit:** favor the idea you're unusually able to win.
cards.callout: **Try it today:** write your next idea in one line. Under it, name three people who already spend time or money on this problem.
